3. The investigation of that Gulshan PS Case No. 73 dated 24-4-1998 under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code was ultimately taken up by Md Mojibur Rahman, an assistant superintendent of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) the PW 1. After completion of investigation this Investigating Officer submitted charge-sheet in that Gulshan PS Case No.73 dated 24-4-1998 under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code against accused Shahidul Islam alias Shahid, Sayed Sajjad Mainuddin Hasan alias Hasan, Humayun Kabir alias Humayun, Badal, Shaniram Mondal, Parveen and Estema Khatun alias Minu and he, being informant, lodged a separate FIR with Gulshan Police Station on 4-9-1998 under the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995 with respect to the same occurrence implicating all the charge-sheeted accused persons of that Gulshan PS Case No.73 dated 24-4-1998 as accused. In that FIR the informant CID officer stated to the effect that during investigation of the Gulshan PS Case No. 73 dated 24-4-1998 accused Shahid, Humayun Kabir, Minu and Parveen made statements under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and that these statements, the post mortem report of the dead body of the deceased and other information's revealed that accused Sajjad Mainuddin Hasan alias Hasan (hereinafter referred to as Hasan) hatched up a conspiracy and engaged the other accused persons to murder Shajneen after committing rape on her to retaliate an incident that took Place on 1-4-1998; that accused Hasan is a Diploma Engineer and he was engaged by victim's father Latifur Rahman for the renovation works of his house two years back and Hasan had easy access to every part of that house (hereinafter referred to as PO house). That taking advantage of his position Hasan, at about 3.30 pm, on 1-4-1998, entered into victim Shajneen's bedroom and asked her to go inside her bathroom to show him the defective mirror which required to be replaced. That Shajneen then went inside the bathroom to show Hasan the defective mirror, but at that time Hasan grabbed Shajneen with an ill motive to which Shajneen reacted sharply and came out of the bathroom and threatened Hasan to give him a lesson by informing her parents. At this Hasan felt very insulted and came out from the bathroom in an angry mood. That this incident (hereinafter referred to as the bathroom incident) led Hasan to hatch a conspiracy to wipe out Shajneen from the scenario. So, Hasan engaged the other accused persons, namely Shahid, Badal, Humayun Kabir alias Humayun, Shaniram Mondal, Parveen and Estema Khatun alias Minuall of whom were servants and employees of the PO house-to execute that conspiracy. However, Shajneen did not disclose the bathroom incident immediately to her parents, because Shajneen herself and her two elder sisters Simeen Hossain and Shahreh Huq Sheji (PWs 3 and 4) along with some servants were scheduled to go to Marina Tea Garden under Kulaura Police Station within District Moulovibazar for a pleasure trip on the next day i.e. on 2-4-1998 and also because her parents were taking preparation at that time for going to Shilong in India on 3-4-1998. However, after going to Tea Garden Shajneen, on 3-4-1998, disclosed the bathroom incident to her elder sisters and 3/4 days thereafter to their husbands also when they reached the Tea Garden on 7-4-1998. The sisters and their husbands then took a decision to report about that bathroom incident to their parents who were scheduled to return from Shilong, India on 18-4-1998. Shajneen, her sisters and their husbands returned to Dhaka on 16-4-1998 and Shajneen stayed at her sister Simeen's house till 18-4-1998 when their parents arrived and took Shajneen to the PO House. However, the disclosure of the bathroom incident was delayed, because after arrival from India, Shajneen's mother became ill and her father became busy with his business. So, the elder sisters and their husbands decided to disclose the bathroom incident to their parents on 24-4-1998, Friday, when they would meet together at lunch. That Hasan could sense the upcoming disclosure and the potential danger. So, he selected the party time in the evening hours of 23-4-1998 to execute the conspiracy and activated the other accused persons and accordingly accused Shahid, with the aid and assistance of other accused persons committed rape and murder of Shajneen. 

 5. The case was ultimately sent to the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Bishesh Adalat No.2, Dhaka and was registered as Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Special Case No. 43 of 1999 which was subsequently re-numbered as Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Special Case No. 404 of 2002. The Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Bishesh Adalat (hereinafter referred to as Adalat) held trial after framing formal charges under section 6(1) and 6(2) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995 (hereinafter referred to as Ain of 1995) against condemned prisoner Shahid and under sections 6(1)/14 and 6(2)/14 of the Ain of 1995 against accused Hasan, Badal, Shaniram Mondal, Parveen and Estema Khatun alias Minu. Accused Humayun Kabir alias Humayun died before framing of charge. 

 6. The prosecution examined 22 witnesses out of 74 charge-sheeted witnesses before the Bishesh Adalat. The accused persons did not examine any witness. The Adalat, on consideration of evidence adduced by the prosecution, found accused Shahid guilty under section 6(2) of the Ain of 1995 and the other accused persons under sections 6(2)/14 of that Ain of 1995 and sentenced all of them to death by the judgment and order dated 2-9-2003, as already mentioned before. The Adalat made a Reference to the High Court Division for confirmation of death sentences awarded against all the accused persons on the basis of which the above mentioned Death Reference No. 98 of 2003 was started. All the 6 condemned prisoners filed 6(six) separate petitions of appeal from jail against the judgment and order of conviction and sentences passed by the Adalat and the Jail authority forwarded those 6 jail petitions jointly to the High Court Division and all those 6 (six) jail petitions were registered as one appeal, being Jail Appeal No. 184 of 2004. The condemned prisoner Hasan filed a regular appeal also, being Criminal Appeal No. 6344 of 2003 before the High Court Division. A Division Bench of the High Court Division heard the Death. Reference along with the Jail Appeal No. 184 of 2004 and Criminal Appeal No. 3644 of 2003 together and by the impugned judgment and order affirmed the conviction and sentences of death of all the condemned prisoners except condemned prisoner Shaniram Mandal only as already mentioned above. The High Court Division found that the evidence of prosecution witnesses, specially the PWs 3, 4, 5, 7, 12 and 13 coupled with the confessional statement of accused Shahid and the statements of accused Minu and Parvin under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure proved the charges against all the condemned prisoners except accused Shaniram Mondal only beyond all reasonable doubt. 

 7. Against this impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division the condemned prisoner Sayed Sajjad Mainuddin Hasan alias Hasan preferred Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 102 of 2007 before this Division and this Division granted leave to appeal, being Criminal Appeal No. 38 of 2009, to consider the submissions made by the learned Counsel for the leave-petitioner to the effect that there was no reliable evidence at all to prove that the condemned leave-petitioner instigated or abetted the commission of rape and murder of the victim in any way, that the High Court Division did not consider at all the statements of accused Shahid made under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and also in his first confessional statements where he stated that he alone committed the offence and that save and except the so-called 2nd confessional statement of co-accused Shahid there is no legal evidence at all to prove the complicity of the condemned prisoner Hasan in the alleged occurrence and that the alleged bathroom incident of 1-4-1998 has not been proved by any reliable and convincing evidence at all to connect this accused petitioner with the alleged crime inasmuch as the prosecution witnesses 3, 4 and 5, who deposed before the Court in support of that alleged bathroom incident, though claimed that they heard about that incident from Shajneen, they did not disclose the said incident before the death of victim Shajneen nor even at the time of lodging of the FIR by the father of the victim Shajneen and did not disclose the same until 2-5.1998, which creates a serious doubt about the prosecution case and also supports the defence version that the condemned petitioner Hasan was implicated in this case long after the occurrence falsely with ill motive. 

 8. The other condemned prisoners Badal, Parvin, Eshtema Khatun alias Minu filed the above mentioned Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 230 of 2009 and these 3 condemned prisoners and also the condemned prisoners Shahidul Islam alias Shahid and Hasan filed separate jail petitions which were forwarded to this Court by the Jail authority jointly and on the basis of those the Jail Petition No. 13 of 2003 was registered. 

 9. Mr Khondker Mahbub Hossain, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the condemned prisoners has made submissions before us to the effect that in this case both the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Bishesh Adalat and the High Court Division have committed wrong, illegality and grave injustice in convicting the accused Hasan and other accused persons in the absence of any reliable evidence at all. The learned Advocate has contended that in this case there is no reliable and acceptable evidence at all to prove the complicity of the accused-appellant Hasan and other condemned accused Badal, Parvin and Minu in the alleged offence. The learned Advocate has argued that the accused Shahid, within a few days of the alleged occurrence, made confessional statement before a Magistrate, 1st Class, implicating himself only in the rape and murder of the victim Shajneen and this accused in the last stage of trial of the case also made statement under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure stating that he himself alone, and no other accused person, was involved in the murder of victim Shajneen, but the tribunal and the High Court Division did not take into consideration this statement of the accused Shahid at all, that they most illegally relied upon a so-called second confessional statement of this accused Shahid which was allegedly made long several months after the alleged occurrence, on 28-9-98 and which was retracted later by the confessing accused Shahid; the learned Advocate has argued that this so-called 2nd confessional statement of accused Shahid is not voluntary and true at all, it was obtained by severe torture and that in the facts and circumstances of the case, this 2nd confessional statement of accused Shahid has no evidentiary value at all and the conviction of other accused persons relying mainly on this 2nd retracted confessional statement of co-accused Shahid has been most illegal. The learned Advocate has contended that it is a settled principal of law that unless corroborated by sufficient reliable evidence the confessional statement of co-accused cannot be basis of conviction and sentence of any-accused. The learned Advocate has argued also that though at a belated stage the prosecution has introduced the story of bathroom incident, but this alleged bathroom incident has not been roved at all in this case. The learned Advocate as pointed out that though this alleged bathroom incident allegedly took place on 1-4-1998 but Shajneen, inspite of being furious, as alleged, did not tell about that bathroom incident to her mother even who was at that very time in that house, and also to her father and sisters within a long period, that though Shajneen allegedly disclosed that bathroom incident to her sisters and sisters husbands several days after that bathroom incident but even then also her sisters, their husbands and she herself did not disclose that bathroom incident to her parents and that even after the rape and murder of Shajneen her sisters and sisters' husbands did not disclose that bathroom incident to her parents until 2-5-1998. The learned Advocate has argued that this fact of non-disclosure of the alleged bathroom incident to the parents of victim Shajneen within a long period by anybody including Shajneen and even within a long period of 8/9 days after the murder of Shajneen by her sisters and their husbands-very reasonably makes this alleged bathroom incident unbelievable. The learned Advocate has argued to the effect also that in fact the story of this alleged bathroom incident has been manufactured subsequently only to implicate this accused appellant Hasan and the other condemned prisoners in the rape and murder of Shajneen. The learned Advocate has argued that both the Adalat and the High Court Division committed wrong and illegality in believing this story of bathroom incident without taking into consideration at all the acceptability and reliability of the evidence adduced by the prosecution to prove this alleged bathroom incident. The learned Advocate has argued that save and except this alleged bathroom incident there is no evidence at all or no reason at all to connect this accused appellant Hasan with the rape and murder of Shajneen, a minor girl of 15 years. The learned Advocate has argued also that this accused appellant Hasan is aged more than 50 years having children of the age of victim Shajneen and that there is no reason at all and no fact has been proved at all to implicate this accused appellant in the rape and murder of Shajneen. Mr Khondker Mahbub Hossain, the learned Senior Advocate for the accused appellant has argued to the effect also that the Adalat and the High Court Division have committed illegality in relying on the evidence of a most unreliable witness, the PW 12 Sufia who has been procured by the police at a very belated stage in order to prove the prosecution case that this accused Hasan engaged the other convicted accused namely Badal, Parvin and Minu to assist the accused Shahid in committing rape and murder of the deceased Shajneen. The learned Advocate has elaborated his argument stating that this PW 12 Sufia though deposed before the tribunal to the effect that a few days before the occurrence she was told by the accused Minu and Parvin that accused Hasan made a plan to cause rape and murder of Shajneen by the accused Shahid, Badal, Humayun and Shaniram and subsequently on that very day accused Hasan also told her that what she heard from Minu and Parvin was true and threatened her also not to disclose that to anybody, but this PW 12 Sufia did not disclose this alleged fact of her knowing about the alleged conspiracy to anybody before the occurrence and even within a long period after the occurrence. The learned Advocate has contended that this very belated disclosure of this very terrifying information by the PW 12 not only make this witness unreliable but also tells reasonably that this witness has been procured subsequently by the police in order to prove the charges against the accused persons. The learned Advocate has argued that this PW 12 is not at all a reliable witness but inspite of that both the tribunal and the High Court Division have relied on the evidence of this very much unreliable witness and found that the evidence of this PW 12 have corroborated the second confessional statement of accused Shahid. The learned Advocate has argued that the evidence of this PW 12 being not reliable at all the so-called second confessional statement of co-accused Shahid remained uncorroborated and in the circumstances the conviction and sentences of the accused-appellant and other accused-petitioners on the basis of so-called second confessional statement of accused Shahid has been most illegal. The learned Advocate has made argument to the effect also that in this case it has not been proved beyond doubt also that victim Shajneen was raped before murder. The learned Advocate has pointed out that in the postmortem examination report of the victim it has been stated that no spermatozoa was found in the virginal swab of the victim and the accused Shahid also, in his statement under section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code told to the effect that though he murdered Shajneen, but he did not rape her. The learned Advocate has contended that this statement of accused Shahid under section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code and the postmortem examination report of the dead body of the victim prove that victim Shajneen was not raped before murder. It has also been argued from the side of the condemned prisoners that in this case though charge was framed against the condemned prisoners under sections 6(1) and 6(1)/14 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995, but the condemned prisoners have been convicted and sentenced under sections 6(2) and 6(2)/14 of the said Ain, which provides graver punishment and that for this reason also the conviction and sentence are not sustainable. 

 10. Mr Khondker Mahbub Hossain has concluded his argument making submission to the effect that this accused appellant Hasan and the other condemned prisoners Badal, Parveen and Minu, inspite of being innocent, have been languishing in the condemned cell for long 18 years. 

 11. Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned Attorney-General for the State-respondent and Mr Nozrul Islam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the informant have made submissions refuting the argument made by the learned Advocate for the condemned appellant and other condemned prisoners. Their arguments are that in this case the rape and murder of the victim Shajneen have been proved beyond all reasonable doubt by sufficient evidence including the postmortem examination report of the dead body of the victim; that the confessional statement of accused Shahid is very much voluntary and true and this confessional statement of this accused Shahid coupled with the evidence of PWs 2, 3, 4, 5, 12 and 13 have proved sufficiently the prosecution case that the accused appellant Hasan, being threatened by Shajneen for his attempt to make illicit relation with her, made the conspiracy to cause rape and murder of Shajneen and engaged the other condemned prisoners to cause rape and murder of Shajneen. The learned Attorney-General has made submission to the effect also that the reasons of delayed disclosure of the bathroom incident by the PWs 3, 4 and 5 have been well explained in this case and that the Adalat and the High Court Division, considering this explanation as to delay in disclosure of this bathroom incident, rightly believed this bathroom incident. The learned Attorney-General has pointed out that the evidence of PWs 2 and 3 have proved that on 21-4-1998 and 23-4-1998 Shajneen, seeing Hasan, reacted and angrily said that she would punish Hasan by telling her parents about that bathroom incident and has argued that these incidents of 21-4-1998 and 23-4-1998, which have been well proved by the evidence of PWs 3 and 4, lend support to the bathroom incident and as such the Adalat and the High Court Division committed no wrong at all in believing the bathroom incident. As regards the testimony of the PW 12 Sufia the argument of the learned Advocates for the State-respondent and the informant is that Sufia stated clearly before the Adalat that she was threatened by accused Hasan and Badal not to disclose about that conspiracy to any body and in that circumstances it was very much natural for her, a poor lady, not to disclose that conspiracy to any body and that only after arrest of accused Hasan and accused Badal she disclosed about that conspiracy and in the circumstances, there is no reason for disbelieving her and that the Adalat and the High Court Division, therefore, rightly relied on the evidence of the PW 12. The learned Advocates have pointed out also that evidence of PW 13-Muslim Howlader, another employee of PO house, has corroborated the evidence of PW 12. The learned Advocates have made argument to the effect also that besides accused Shahid, Minu also made a confessional statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on 31-7-1998 implicating accused Hasan, Humayun and Shahid in the alleged occurrence of rape and murder of Shajneen and this confessional statement of accused Minu lend support to the confessional statement of the accused Shahid. The learned Advocates have pointed out also that the postmortem examination report of the dead body of Shajneen shows that there were as many as 23 injuries caused by sharp cutting weapons on the dead body which reasonably indicates that more than one assailant was involved in the murder of Shajneen. The learned Advocates have contended that this fact proves that in the first confessional statement of accused Shahid he suppressed some facts and this fact proves also that the second confessional statement of the accused Shahid was true. The learned Advocates have pointed out that it is in evidence that on 2-5-1998 accused Hasan was found in the CID Office inquiring about accused Shahid and have contended that this fact also lends support to the prosecution case that the accused Hasan made the conspiracy and accused Shahid and others executed that conspiracy by committing rape and murder of Shajneen. The learned Attorney-General and the learned Advocate Mr Nozrul Islam Chowdhury have argued that the High Court Division did not commit any wrong in affirming the conviction and sentences of the accused appellant and other condemned petitioners awarded by the Adalat and in the circumstances, this criminal appeal and also the criminal petition for leave to appeal and the jail petition are liable to be dismissed. 

 15. The prosecution's case is that before murder Shajneen was raped and to prove this case also the prosecution adduced sufficient evidence before the Adalat. But from the side of the defence, it was argued before the Adalat and also before the High Court Division and before this Division that the alleged rape of Shajneen before her murder has not been proved in this case. Obviously, the defence has raised this plea in view of the postmortem examination report of the dead body of Shajneen and also the statement of accused Shahid which he made under section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code. In the post-mortem examination report-the exhibit-8 it has been stated that no spermatozoa was found in the vaginal swab of the victim and in his 342 statement accused Shahid claimed that he did not rape Shajneen though he murdered her. 

 18. PW 17 Dr. Belayet Hossain Khan, one of the members of the Medical Board which held postmortem examination on the dead body of the victim, also has deposed before the Adalat to the effect that the victim was raped before murder. In the inquest report also, the exhibit-4, there is mention to the effect that semen was found on the thigh and vagina of the victim. The evidence of PWs 2, 3 and 4, the father and two elder sisters of the victim also indicate that victim was subjected to rape before murder. These prosecution witnesses have stated before the Adalat to the effect that they saw the dead body of the victim lying on the floor of her bedroom almost in naked condition. They stated to the effect that there was no clothes on the lower part of the body of the victim and that her wearing black "panty" was found pulled down below the knees. The PW 3, who was also present at the time of holding inquest on the dead body, deposed to the effect also that she saw semen on the thigh and vagina of the victim. Apart from these above evidence there are other evidence also which directly tell that victim was raped before her murder. The accused Shahid has made two confessional statements and in both those confessional statements he confessed to the effect that he committed rape on the victim. Shajneen before causing her death. All the above mentioned evidence the post-mortem examination report, the inquest report, the evidence of PWs 2, 3 and 4 and the confessional statement of accused Shahid himself prove beyond any doubt that victim was raped before murder. 

 19. The observations in the postmortem examination report to the effect that no spermatozoa was found in the vaginal swab of the victim does not prove at all that victim was not raped before her murder, because presence of spermatozoa is not at all necessary to prove rape (vide Moinul Haque vs State 56 DLR (AD) 81). It has been settled by so many decisions of the apex courts of this region that even complete penetration is not essential to constitute rape and even partial penetration with or without emission of semen and rupture of hymen is sufficient to constitute rape. It may be mentioned here that section 2(1) or the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995 has explained 'rape' thus: “ধর্ষণ শব্দটি ” Penal Code (Act XLV of 1860)- এর  section 375 এ উল্লিখিত  "rape" “শব্দটির ন্যায় একই অর্থ বহন করিবে ”। According to section 375 of Penal Code mere penetration is sufficient to constitute rape. 

 20. Accused Shahid in his 342 statement, evidently tried to conceal this fact of rape though in his own earlier two confessional statements he narrated elaborately how he caused rape to victim Shajneen. Considering all the above mentioned evidence including the own confessional statements of this accused Shahid both the tribunal and the High Court Division did not give any reliance on this very belated statement of accused Shahid which he made under section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code and rightly found that victim Shajneen was raped before murder. Considering all the above mentioned evidence we also find that in this case it has been proved beyond all reasonable doubt that victim Shajneen was raped before murder. The contention of the learned Advocate for the condemned prisoners that rape of victim Shajneen has not been proved in this case is not entertainable at all. 

 21. Before examining the propriety of the conviction and sentences of condemned prisoners Hasan, Badal, Parveen and Minu we find it convenient to examine the propriety of the conviction and sentence of accused Shahid separately first. 

 22. This accused Shahid aged about 20/21 years was a, servant of the PO house since 11/2 years before the occurrence. In the first FIR lodged by the father of the victim immediately after the occurrence this Shahid was suspected as the rapist and murderer. In the first FIR it was alleged that this Shahid was found absconding after detection of murder and rape of the victim in that very night and suspicion was also expressed to the effect that this Shahid might have murdered the victim after committing rape on her. Within a few days of lodging of that FIR this accused Shahid himself surrendered to police at Chittagong on 27-4-1998 and he was then handed over to police of Gulshan Police Station, Dhaka on the same date. Thereafter on 13-5-1998 this accused Shahid made a confessional statement before a Magistrate, 1st Class which has been marked in this case as B/I. We find it necessary to reproduce the relevant portion of this confessional statement of accused Shahid here: 

 24. These above quoted two confessional statements of accused Shahid coupled with the other evidence adduced by the prosecution, as mentioned above, prove sufficiently that accused Shahid raped victim Shajneen before causing her murder. Long several years after making of this confessional statement accused Shahid, during his examination under section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code, has claimed that he did not rape Shajneen though he murdered her. But in view of his own confessional statement reproduced above, specially his first confessional statement-the very narration of which tells that it was made spontaneously, we are unable to give any reliance on his very belated statement which he made under section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code. In his first confessional statement this accused stated how he felt tempted to rape Shajneen, He stated thus: 

 25. Apart from the confessional statements of accused Shahid the prosecution has adduced other sufficient evidence to prove that Shajneen was raped before her murder and we have already found that these evidence adduced by the prosecution have proved sufficiently that Shajneen was raped before her murder. Accused Shahid has all through admitted that he murdered Shajneen. In his statement under section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code also accused Shahid has clearly stated that he murdered Shajneen. In the circumstances the above stated confessional statements of accused Shahid coupled with the proven fact that victim Shajneen was subjected to rape before murder prove beyond any doubt that accused Shahid raped and murdered Shajneen. So, the Adalat rightly convicted and sentenced accused Shahid under section 6(2) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995 and the High Court Division rightly confirmed this conviction and sentence of accused Shahid. 

 26. Now about the other 4 condemned prisoners Hasan, Badal, Estema Khatun @ Minu and Parveen. To connect these four accused persons with the rape and murder of victim Shajneen the prosecution's case is that accused Hasan, a Sub-Assistant Engineer, who was engaged for the renovation works of PO house two years before the occurrence, developed some grudge against the victim Shajneen and this accused Hasan hatched a conspiracy with other accused persons to cause rape and murder of victim Shajneen. The prosecution's case is that on 1-4-1998, at about 3-00 pm accused Hasan entered into the bedroom of the victim Shajneen and asked her to go inside the bathroom to show him the defective mirror which required to be replaced and victim Shajneen then went inside the bathroom to show the accused Hasan the defective mirror and at that time accused Hasan grabbed her with ill motive and at this Shajneen reacted sharply and she came out of the bathroom and threatened Hasan that she would punish Hasan by informing her parents about that occurrence and that accused Hasan then, being angry, went out of the room of the victim Shajneen and thereafter he, to take revenge upon Shajneen, hatched the conspiracy with other accused persons to cause rape and murder of victim and accordingly he selected 23-4-1998, when a party was scheduled to be held on the 1st floor of PO house, as the date of execution of that conspiracy and engaged the other accused persons including accused Shahid to cause rape and murder of Shajneen and accordingly accused Shahid with the assistance of other accused persons raped and murdered victim Shajneen. 

 27. To prove this case the prosecution has relied on the evidence of PWs 2, 3, 4, 5, 12 and 13. The PW 2 is the father of the victim. The PWs 3 and 4 are two elder sisters of the victim and the PW 5 is the husband of PW 4. The PW 12 is maid servant of PW 3 and PW 13 is the servant of PW 2. 

 28. The PWs 3 and 4 have deposed to the effect that Shajneen told them about the bathroom incident on 3-4-1998 in the tea garden in Kulaura, Moulovibazar and PW 5 stated to the effect that on his arrival at that tea garden Shajneen informed him about that bathroom incident on 7-4-1998. From the side of the defence objection has been raised as to the admissibility of the evidence of these PWs 3, 4 and 5 contending that their such evidence are hearsay evidence and as such these are not admissible in evidence. The defence argu-ment is that none of these 3 prosecution witnesses witnessed the alleged bathroom incident on 1-4-1998 and that what they stated about that bathroom incident were therefore hearsay evidence as they heard about that incident from Shajneen. 

 30. Section 32(1) of the Evidence Act has provided some exceptions to this general rule of exclusion of hearsay evidence. 

 "32. Cases in which statement of relevant fact by person who is dead or cannot be found, etc, is relevant-Statements, written or verbal, of relevant facts made by a person who is dead, or who cannot be found, or who has become incapable of giving evidence, or whose attendance cannot be procured without an amount of delay or expense which under the circumstances of the case appears to the Court unreasonable, are themselves relevant fact in the following cases: 

 31. The above quoted section 32(1) of the Evidence Act has made any statement, written or verbal, of a dead person admissible in evidence when these statements are as regards any facts and circumstances which resulted in his/her death irrespective of the fact whether the person who made those statements was under expectation of death or not at the time of making those statements. In the present case the prosecution's case is that the said bathroom incident led accused Hasan to hatch the conspiracy to cause rape and murder of the victim Shajneen and resultantly she was raped and murdered. So, to take the evidence of PWs 3, 4 and 5 as to this bathroom incident in evidence the prosecution has to prove that being enraged by this bathroom incident accused Hasan made conspiracy to cause rape and murder of victim Shajneen and consequently Shajneen was raped and murdered. 

 32. However, mere admissibility of any evidence does not make that evidence true or believable. To rely on any evidence the court has to be sure about the truth or genuineness of that evidence. In this case from the side of the defence strong armament has been made to the effect that the evidence of PWs 3, 4 and 5 as to the bathroom incident cannot be relied on at all inasmuch as these witnesses disclosed the alleged fact of their hearing about the bathroom incident from victim Shajneen at a very belated stage, long about one month after hearing of the same and long nine days after the rape and murder of Shajneen. Before considering this argument of the learned Advocate for the condemned prisoners we need to examine what these three PWs deposed before the Adalat. 

 33. The PW 3 Mrs Simeen Hossain (shortly Simeen) and PW 4 Mrs Shazre Haque @ Sheji (hereinafter referred as Sheji)-the elder sisters of the victim Shajneen have deposed to the effect that on 2-4-1998 they along with victim Shajneen and their children went to Marina tea garden at Kulaura, Moulovibazar for a pleasure trip. That on 3-4-1998, in the morning while they were taking tea, Shajneen told them that on 1-4-1998, at about 3-30 pm while she was reading a book inside her room accused Hasan entered that room and told her to show the defective mirror and Shajneen then went inside the bathroom to show that mirror to Hasan and at that time Hasan grabbed Shajneen with ill motive and at this Shajneen got angry and pushed.aside Hasan and told him that she would punish him by telling her parents about that occurrence and at this Hasan angrily went out of the room of Shajneen. Both these witnesses deposed also that on 7-4-1998 when their husbands went to that tea garden at Kulaura Shajneen again narrated that bathroom incident to them. The PW 5 Arshadul Hug, the husband of PW 4 Sheji deposed corroborating the PWs 3 and 4. This witness deposed to the effect that on 7-4-1998 at about 10-00 am in the morning Shajneen informed him and his brother-in-law Waker (the husband of PW 3 Simeen) about the bathroom incident of 1-4-1998. This witness also narrated that bathroom incident as has been narrated by PWs 3 and 4. All these PWs 3, 4 and 5 deposed to the effect also that being informed about that bathroom incident by victim Shajneen they all took decision that they would inform that bathroom incident to their parents after they returned from Shilong. India; that on 16-4-1998 they came back to Dhaka and all of them stayed at Simeen's house. On 18-4-1998 their parents came back from. Shilong and took away Shajneen from Simeen's house. These witnesses deposed to the effect also that since Simeen's mother was ill at that time they decided to inform their parents about that bathroom incident on 24-4-1998, Friday, after `namaz' when they all would meet at lunch. The PW 3 Simeen has deposed further that on 21-4-1998 she came to her father's house and from there she along with Shajneen went to Gulshan market and before evening they came back from market. That while they entered into the house they saw accused Hasan standing there and seeing Hasan Shajneen got furious and asked him how did he dare to remain standing there and that she (PW 3) then told Shajneen to keep silent and assured her that on 24-4-1998 her parents would punish Hasan. The PW 4 Sheji also deposed further to the effect that on 23-4-1998 a party was scheduled to be held at her father's house and on that day, at about 5 pm, she along with Shajneen went to the 1st floor of the PO house to see the preparation for that party and at that time they saw Hasan standing in the verandah and seeing him Shajneen got furious and told him how could he dare to remain standing there and that she would punish him on the next day telling her parents. The PW 4 deposed also that she then brought down Shajneen to the ground floor. All these PWs 3, 4 and 5 deposed to the effect that they ultimately informed the parents of Shajneen about that bath-room incident on 2-5-1998 (i.e. long nine days after the occurrence). 

 34. The PW 2 Latifur Rahman has deposed before court to the effect that the PWs 3, 4 and 5 informed him about that bathroom incident on 2-5-1998. 

 35. Now we are to consider how far this very belated disclosure of bathroom incident by PWs 3, 4 and 5 can be relied on. From the side of the accused persons strong arguments have been made against the credibility of the above evidence of PWs 3, 4 and 5. It has been argued from the side of the accused persons that non-disclosure of the alleged bathroom incident by the victim Shajneen herself to her parents within a long period and the non-disclosure of the said incident by the PWs 3, 4 and 5 to the parents of the victim Shajneen within a long period even after rape and murder of Shajneen make this very bathroom incident unbelievable. On the contrary, from the side of the prosecution arguments have been made to the effect that the cause of this delayed disclosure of the bathroom incident by the PWs 3, 4 and 5 have been explained in this case, that admittedly the parents of Shajneen went to Shilong, India and after their coming back from there on 18-4-1998 mother of Shajneen became ill and her father became busy with his business and Shajneen and her sisters and their husbands then took decision that they would inform their parents about that bathroom incident on 24-4-1998, Friday when they would all meet at lunch but before that Shajneen was murdered. It has also been argued from the side of the prosecution that the other 2 incidents of 21-4-1998 and 23-4-1998 of Shajneen's reaction seeing Hasan, as revealed from the evidence of PWs 3 and 4, lend support to this bathroom incident. 

 36. We have considered the arguments advanced from both the sides as to the credibility of the story of bathroom incident. Victim Shajneen was the youngest child of Mr and Mrs Latifur Rahman and was very much beloved of them. It is in evidence that on the date of alleged bathroom incident, i.e. on 1-4-1998 victim's mother was at home. She was at home even at the time of alleged bathroom incident, i.e. at 3-30 pm. It is also in evidence that the bedroom of the victim Shajneen was adjacent to the bedroom of her parents. There is no evidence on record that on 1-4-1998 victim's mother was ill. Then why the victim Shajneen did not inform her mother then and there about that bathroom incident. Prosecution's case is that victim Shajneen got furious at that bathroom incident and threatened accused Hasan telling that she would punish him by telling her parents about that behaviour of Hasan. But inspite of her being very much furious for that bathroom incident she did not inform her mother who was then present in the house. It was very much natural that a young girl of 15 years, being such ill treated by an employee of her father, would inform about that ill treatment to her parents, specially to her mother immediately. The non-disclosure of this alleged bathroom incident by Shajneen to her mother even, who was very near to her at that very time, reasonably raises question about the credibility of this bathroom incident. It is in evidence that a full time "Aya" (maid servant) namely, Hawa Bibi was engaged to look after the victim Shajneen and that "Aya" used to sleep inside the victim's room. Victim Shajneen did not tell this "Aya" also about that bathroom incident. It is in evidence that this "Aya" Hawa Bibi was still working in the PO house, but this Hawa Bibi was not produced before court to support this alleged bathroom incident. The fact that this all-time "Aya" of victim Shajneen also could not know anything about that bathroom incident, also, in our opinion, raises suspicion about this bathroom incident. This bathroom incident allegedly was told by the victim Shajneen to her two elder sisters" Simeen and Sheji (PWs 3 and 4) and also their husbands on 3-4-1998 and 7-4-1998 respectively, but these witnesses also did not disclose about that bathroom incident to their parents before 2-5-1998. If we believe that for some inevitable reasons the victim and also the PWs 3, 4 and 5 could not inform their parents about that bathroom incident before the murder of Shajneen on 23-4-1998, but why the PWs 3, 4 and 5 did not inform their parents about that bathroom incident immediate after the murder of Shajneen, why they took long nine days to disclose that bathroom incident to their parents and others. According to the prosecution case the PWs 3, 4 and 5 disclosed about that bathroom incident to their parents only on 2-5-1998. It is in evidence that after murder of Shajneen the accused Hasan came to the PO house on the very next morning, he attended the `janaja' of victim Shajneen and also the `kulkhanr of victim Shajneen which was held on 26-4-1998. It is also in evidence that on 30-4-1998 also the PW 3 Simeen called accused Hasan through PW 7 and accused Hasan came to the PO house on 30-4-1998 and PW 3 Simeen then talked with him, but at that time also the PW 3 or the PWs 4 and 5 did not disclose about that bathroom incident to anybody and did not ask Hasan even any question about that bathroom incident. Argument has been made from the side of the prosecution that the evidence of PWs 3 and 4 have proved that victim Shajneen got furious seeing Hasan in their house on 21-4-1998 and 23-4-1998 and that these facts also lend support to the bathroom incident. But we are unable to accept this argument also of the prosecution. These alleged incidents of 21-4-1998 and 23-4-1998 also were disclosed by P.Ws.3 and 4 at a very belated stage. Moreover it appears that the P.w.4 Sheji did not disclose the alleged incidents of 21-4-1998 and 23-4-1971 to the investigating officer while giving statements under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 37. However, even if it is believed that the alleged bathroom incident and the subsequent alleged incidents of 21-4-1998 and 23-4-1998 are true, can these be considered as conclusive proof of accused Hasan's alleged conspiracy to cause rape and murder of Shajneen? 

 38. To prove the charges against accused Hasan and other accused persons the prosecution must prove that Hasan actually hatched a conspiracy to cause rape and murder of Shajneen and he engaged the other accused persons to execute that conspiracy. It cannot be denied that a conspiracy is hatched in secret and it is difficult to procure direct evidence to prove that conspiracy. In a case of conspiracy the prosecution has to depend mainly on circumstantial evidence. Proof of conspiracy is largely inferential, though the inference must be founded on solid facts and surrounding circumstances. However, in the present case, it appears that the prosecution has adduced some direct evidence to prove the alleged conspiracy allegedly hatched by accused Hasan to cause rape and murder of Shajneen. The prosecution witness No. 12 Sufia has deposed in this case in support of these conspiracy allegedly hatched by accused Hasan. This PW 12 is the maid servant of PW 3 Simeen the elder sister of victim Shajneen. This PW 12 has deposed that she was engaged in the house of Simeen 5 months before the occurrence. She used to come to the house of Simeen's father at Gulshan every morning with the children of Simeen and in the afternoon Simeen used to take her back with her children to her house at Baridhara; that a few days before rape and murder of Shajneen they came back, from Sylhet tea garden and a few days thereafter she came to the house of Simeen's father at Gulshan. At that time she saw Parveen and Minu, the maid servants, in the ironing room. She then told them that Simeen would give them another maid servant named Nurjahan, but at that time Minu and Parveen told her that they did not require any maid servant and told her also that engineer Hasan (the accused Hasan) was making a plan to cause rape and murder of Shajneen to take revenge on her, that they told also that accused Shahid, Badal, Humayun and Shaniram were the trusted persons of accused Hasan and they would execute that plan of accused Hasan. We find it necessary to quote the relevant portion of the evidence of this PW 12 Sufia here. She deposed before the Adalat thus: 

 39. In course of cross-examination this witness has stated clearly that 2 days before the occurrence she heard about that conspiracy and that she did not disclose about that conspiracy to anybody and that 10/12 days after arrest of accused Hasan and Badal she disclosed about that conspiracy to police. 

 40. The PW 13 Moslem Hawlader is another servant of PO house. He deposed to the effect that in the night of occurrence he was serving food in the dining hall of the 1st floor where the party was held and after serving food there he came down to the ground floor and saw that Badal was talking over telephone and he heard that Badal was saying that security lights were off and the other works were done rightly; (সিকিউরিটি লাইট অফ করা হয়েছে এবং বাকী সব কাজ ঠিক) that on his query Badal told that he talked with engineer Hasan. This witness has deposed to the effect also that some days after the occurrence when he came to know that Hasan engaged other accused persons to murder Shajneen he could remember that on 1st April, 1998 he saw Hasan coming out from the bedroom of Shajneen in an angry mood. This witness has deposed also that he remembered that 2 days before the occurrence he found Hasan, Minu, Parveen and PW 12 Sufia talking in the ironing room. 

 41. The prosecution has relied on the evidence of these PWs 12 and 13 to prove the alleged conspiracy allegedly hatched by the accused Hasan to cause rape and murder of Shajneen. We are to consider whether this PW 12 Sufia can be relied on at all. This Sufia is a maid servant of PW 3 Simeen, the elder sister of victim Shajneen. This witness deposed to the effect that 2 days before the occurrence (i.e. on 21-4-1998) Parveen and Minu-the maid servants of PO house told her about that conspiracy of accused Hasan to cause rape and murder of victim Shajneen by the accused Shahid, Badal, Humayun and Shaniram. But this PW 12 did not disclose this fact of her knowing about this extremely terrifying information to anybody within a long period. Her excuse is that as she was threatened by accused Hasan and Badal not to disclose this fact to anybody she did not disclose that out of fear and that 10/12 days after arrest of Hasan and Badal she disclosed about that fact for the first time. We are unable to accept this explanation for the non-disclosure of this alleged fact of conspiracy by this PW 12 within this long period, if the PW 12 could actually know about such conspiracy to commit such a horrifying crime it was very much natural for her to inform her employer Simeen at least about that conspiracy. Even if we accept her plea that due to threatening of accused Hasan and Badal she did not dare to disclose that conspiracy then why she kept silent for long 10/12 days after the arrest also of accused Hasan and Badal. Her contention is that after arrest of accused Hasan and Badal she felt safe and then she disclosed about that conspiracy. Then why she did not disclose about that conspiracy immediately after arrest of accused Hasan and Badal? There is no explanation about this delay. We have examined the evidence of this PW 12 carefully. It appears that this PW 12 has deposed to the effect that accused Minu and Parveen told her about that conspiracy 2 days before the occurrence i.e. on 21-4-1998, but in the confessional statement of accused Minu, which has been marked as exhibit-3A and which the prosecution has relied upon, it has been stated that on 23-4-1998 Hasan first disclosed about that conspiracy to accused Minu. We should quote here the confessional statement of accused Minu the exhibit-3A: 

 42. This accused Minu in her alleged confessional statement, the exhibit-3A, has stated to the effect that on 23-4-1998 only Hasan told her that “শাজনীন এর রুমে খারাপ কাজ করিবে।” meaning thereby that Shajneen would be raped. This accused in her 164 statement did not tell that she knew about that conspiracy since before and that the other accused persons also, beside accused Shahid and Humayun, were involved in that conspiracy. This accused Minu, in her statement under section 164 of the Criminal Procedure Code did not state also that Hasan told them that victim Shajneen would be murdered also. But the PW 12 Sufia, in her statement before court, stated to the effect that this accused Minu and Parveen told her 2 days before the occurrence i.e. on 21-4-1998 that Hasan made a plan to cause both rape and murder of Shajneen by all the accused persons including accused Badal and Shaniram also. Obviously, there are material inconsistencies in the evidence of this PW 12 and the 164 statement of accused Minu, which very reasonably create suspicion about the truth of evidence of PW 12. It also appears that the accused Shahid himself in his 2nd confessional statement, the exahibit-3/l, has stated to the effect that accused Hasan told him to murder Shajneen with the help of accused Humayun and Parveen. In the second confes-sional statement of accused Shahid he did not tell that he was told by accused Hasan to cause rape also of Shajneen. In this confessional statement accused Shahid did not utter also the name of accused Badal and Shaniram. The relevant portion of this 2nd confessional statement of accused Shahid is quoted below: 

 43. Evidently this confessional statement of accused Shahid also contradicts the evidence of PW 12. It further appears that this PW 12 did not state before the 10 that after the occurrence Badal threatened her not to disclose about that conspiracy to anybody which she stated before the Adalat. This PW 12 did not state also to the I/O that she was told by Minu and Parveen that accused Hasan would cause rape and murder of Shajneen. 

 44. Considering all these facts and circumstances we are unable to put any reliance on the evidence of PW 12 Sufia the maid servant of PW 3 Simeen. The long delay in disclosing this alleged fact of her knowing about the conspiracy of accused Hasan to cause rape and Murder of Shajneen by the other accused persons coupled with the fact that the 164 statements of accused Minu and also Shahid do not corroborate the evidence this PW 12, in our opinion, reasonably make the evidence of PW 12 unbelievable. It cannot be believed that knowing about this very much horrifying news of making plan of causing rape and murder of Shajneen the younger sister of her employer Simeen, the PW 12 would not disclose that to anybody for a long period. This PW 12 has stated "further before the Adalat that she told Nurjahan not to be engaged in the PO house as any incident might take place in that house anytime, but inspite of that Nurjahan came to the PO house on the next day. The prosecution could not examine this Nurjahan to support the evidence of the PW 12. This fact also makes the evidence of PW 12 doubtful. 

 45. The evidence of PW 13 Muslem Howlader, as has been narrated above, is not of much value for the prosecution. As regards the alleged conspiracy his evidence is only that 2 day's before the occurrence .he saw accused Hasan, Minu, Parveen and PW 12 Sufia talking inside the ironing room. These mere statements of P.W. 13 does not tell even that this PW 13 knew anything about the alleged conspiracy to cause rape and murder of Shajneen. Where we have found the evidence of PW 12 not believable, the above evidence of PW 13 is of no help for the prosecution. This PW 13 has deposed also to the effect that in the night of occurrence he found accused Badal telling accused Hasan over telephone that the security lights were off and all other works were done correctly. But we have already pointed out above that in the confessional statements of accused Shahid-on which the prosecution has relied much, the name of this accused Badal has not been uttered even. In the 164 statement of accused Minu also the name of this accused Badal has not been mentioned. The PW 12 Sufia only deposed before the Adalat that on the next night of occurrence accused Badal threatened her not to disclose about that conspi-racy to anybody. But we have already pointed out that this PW 12 did not state this very fact of threatening by accused Badal to the investigation officer. Considering these facts we find that this above statement of PW 13 “সিকিউরিটি লাইট অফ করা হয়েছে এবং বাকি সব কাজ ঠিক” allegedly said by accused Badal to accused Hasan over telephone, even if, is believed as true, then also this statement alone does not prove at all that accused Hasan hatched a conspiracy to cause rape and murder of victim Shajneen and accused Badal also was involved in that conspiracy. 

 46. We have already pointed out above that in the first confessional statement of accused Shahid and in the statements of accused Minu and Parveen which they made under section 164 of the Criminal Procedure Code immediately after the occurrence there is nothing disclosing any conspiracy to cause rape and murder of Shajneen. In those statements, except accused Shahid only, none of the other accused persons was named even. In the second confessional statement of accused Shahid which was made long several months after the occurrence though Shahid named. Hasan as conspirator and other two accused Parveen and Humayun only as the executors of that conspiracy, there is no other reliable evidence at all to support the second confessional statement of accused Shahid. The 164 statement of accused Minu as quoted above, in our opinion, cannot be accepted as a confessional statement as in that confessional statement she did not implicate herself in the rape and murder of Shajneen, she stated only that being threatened by accused Hasan she remained standing in front of dining room and saw accused Shahid and Humayun enter into the bedroom of Shajneen. 

 48. The second confessional statement of accused Shahid though has been accepted by the Adalat and also the High Court Division as voluntary and true, we are unable to accept this second confessional statement of accused Shahid as voluntary and true. Accused Shahid, imme-diately after making of this second confessional statement, filed application retracting the said second confessional statement and also stating that what he stated in his 1st confessional statement was true. During trial of the case the accused Shahid, in his 342 statement, again disowned this second confessional statement stating to the effect that he alone murdered Shajneen and no other accused person was involved in that occurrence. At the time of hearing of this appeal before this Division the learned Advocate for the condemned prisoners has also pointed out that in the first confessional statement this accused Shahid put his signature but in the second confessional statement there is no signature of accused Shahid, rather his LTI was taken in that second confessional statement. The learned Advocate has contended that since the second confessional statement was obtained from Shahid against his will he denied to put his signature in that confessional statement and as such his LTI was obtained forcefully there. The learned Advocate has argued that this fact that in the earlier confessional statement this accused Shahid put his signature and in the second confessional statement, not his signature, but his LTI was obtained-proves that this second confessional statement was not true and voluntary at all. We have considered this argument of the learned Advocate for the condemned prisoners along with the fact that immediate after making this 2nd confessional statement accused Shahid filed an application retracting this second confessional statement and he again disowned this 2nd confessional statement during his examination under section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code. Moreover these two confessions cannot go together. There are conflicting statements-if we believe the first one, we cannot believe the second one. We have drawn the attention of the learned Attorney-General to this inconsistency, but he failed to give any satisfactory explanation and left the matter to be decided by this court upon evaluation of same. This second confession was recorded after 5 months 3 days of surrender of the confessing accused. PW 1 admitted that before recording confession he took accused to PO house on 27-9-1998. Considering all these and also the first confessional statement of accused Shahid, which has been quoted earlier, we refrain from putting reliance on the second confessional statement of accused Shahid. We have already stated earlier that first confessional statement of accused Shahid was very much spontaneous and the narration made in that first confessional statement is also very much convincing. In that first confessional statement accused Shahid narrated elaborately how he felt tempted to have sexual intercourse with the victim Shajneen and how he took the opportunity of the party-time to fulfill his such lust for sex with Shajneen and how he, apprehending resistance from Shajneen, took a sharp cutting knife with him and how he, being resisted by Shajneen in his attempt to commit rape on her, inflicted so many blows with that sharp cutting knife on the different parts of the body of Shajneen. This very elaborate and spontaneous narration in the first confessional statement of accused Shahid makes us convinced about the truth of this first confessional statement. Considering this very first confessional statement of accused Shahid and other facts and circum-stances we are inclined to believe that what accused Shahid stated in his first confessional statement were the real facts and that the cause behind the rape and murder of Shajneen was only the lust for sex of accused Shahid with her. 

 51. The prosecution though has tried to prove its case that accused Hasan had grudge against Shajneen and out of that grudge he made a conspiracy with other accused persons to cause rape and murder of Shajneen and as a result of that conspiracy Shajneen was raped and murdered, but the evidence of the witnesses whom the pro-secution has examined to prove its case cannot be relied on for the reasons as we have pointed out above. Except the PWs 3, 4, 5, 12 and 13 whose evidence we have discussed above-the other prosecution witnesses did not give any evidence supporting the alleged conspiracy. 

 54. The PW 6 is a relation of PW 2 who came to the PO house knowing about the occurrence. This witness however, deposed stating subsequent conduct of accused Hasan. He has deposed to the effect that in the night of occurrence this accused Hasan inspite of getting telephone calls from P.W.7, did not come to the PO house on that night and in the next morning at 7/7-30 P.M. accused Hasan came to PO house being unusually well-dressed and that thereafter he did not find accused Hasan at the janaza' of deceased Shajneen. 

 55. The PW 7, another relation of PW 2 also did not state anything as to the alleged conspiracy. This witness also gave evidence stating some subsequent conduct of accused Hasan. He deposed to the effect that in the very night of occurrence he made two telephone calls to the accused Hasan, one at 12-00 pm and another at 3/3-30 am which were received by the wife of Hasan and that inspite of his request Hasan did not came to the PO house in that very night. This PW 7 deposed further to the effect that in the night of occurrence some guests (the PW 8 and PW 10) interrogated the maid servants Minu and Parveen but they made inconsistent statements. 

 57. The PW 9 is a friend of PW 2 Latifur Rahman. This witness also did not say anything about the alleged conspiracy allegedly hatched by accused Hasan. 

 58. The PW 10, another friend of PW 2 also was one of the invitees in the party of PO house held in night of occurrence. This witness has deposed to the effect that reaching the PO house in the night of occurrence to attend the party he noticed that the security lights of that house were off. This witness also has deposed to the effect that on their interrogation the two maid servants of PO house, namely, Minu and Parveen made inconsistent statements. 

 59. The PW 11 is another friend of PW 2 who deposed to the effect that he came to know about occurrence from newspaper. This witness also did not have any knowledge about the alleged conspiracy allegedly hatched by accused Hasan. 

 62. So, it appears that to prove the charge against accused Hasan, Badal, Minu and Parveen the prosecution has relied on the evidence of PWs 3, 4, 5, 12 and 13 only whose evidence we have already discussed above. We have observed earlier assigning reasons that the evidence of PWs 3, 4 and 5 regarding the bathroom incident cannot be relief on safely. There is no other convincing evidence to support the evidence of these PWs 3, 4 and 5. The PW 13 Muslem Howlader, a servant of the PO house though has deposed before court that subsequently when he came to know that accused Hasan was involved in causing rape and murder of victim Shajneen he could remember that on 1-4-1998 he saw accused Hasan coming out of the bedroom of Shajneen angrily, but we do not find this very belated statement of PW 13 convincing enough to corroborate the evidence of PWs 3, 4 and 5. 

 63. The evidence of PW 12, which only has been relied upon by the prosecution to prove the alleged conspiracy of accused Hasan with the other accused persons, also is not trustworthy for the reasons we have already stated earlier. The prosecution though has tried to add some corroboration to the evidence of this PW 12 by examinipg the aforesaid PW 13 Muslem Howlader, a servant of the PO house, but we have already observed earlier that the evidence of this PW 13 does not lend any support to the evidence of PW 12. 

 64. In a case of conspiracy the conduct of suspected conspirators also are considered important for drawing inference as to the alleged conspiracy. In this case the prosecution has tried to prove some subsequent conduct of accused Hasan and contended that these conducts of accused Hasan also reasonably lead us to the inference that accused Hasan hatched the conspiracy with other accused persons to cause rape and murder of Shajneen. These alleged conducts of accused Hasan, which have been pointed out before us, are that 

 (i) accused Hasan inspite of getting two telephone calls from the PO house conveying the murder of Shajneen did not come to the PO house in that very night of occurrence; 

 65. The prosecution's argument is that these subsequent conducts of accused Hasan reasonably indicate that he was involved in the rape and murder of Shajneen. But we are unable to accept this argument of the prosecution. The accused Hasan, allegedly, was telephoned in the night of occurrence at 12-00 pm and 3-30 am. In that later part of the night accused Hasan could not come to the PO house, but he came to the PO house early in the next morning. It is in evidence that accused Hasan, being asked, told that as his motorcycle was not in order he could not come in that night. We find this reason of accused Hasan's non-coming to the PO house in the mid-night quite acceptable. It should be mentioned here that accused Hasan was not an employee of the PO house, rather he was a contractor engaged by Mr Latifur Rahman for the renovation works of his house. So, like other whole-time employees of Mr Latifur Rahman this accused Hasan was not supposed to remain present in the PO house whole-time or being called, to come to PO house at any time. However, this accused Hasan, admittedly came to the PO house early in the next morning at 7-00/7-30 am. It is also in evidence that accused Hasan attended the `janaja' of Shajneen and also the `kulkhani' which was held on 26-4-1998 and being called by PW 3 Simeen, he came to PO house on 30-4-1998 also. 

 66. We are unable to understand what the prosecution wanted to mean by pointing out that accused Hasan came to PO house in the next morning being "unusually well-dressed." 

 67. The prosecution has argued also that this accused Hasan went to CID office on 2-5-1998 to enquire about accused Shahid who was then in the custody of CID and has contended that this conduct of accused Hasan indicates reasonably that he made conspiracy with accused Shahid and other accused persons to cause rape and murder of Shajneen. But we do not find any cogent evidence to prove that actually accused Hasan went to CID office on 2-5-1998 for making enquiry about accused Shahid. Only the PW 1, the informant and also the 10 of this case the most interested witness has deposed before the Adalat that accused Hasan went to CID office to enquire about accused Shahid. But without any corrobo-ration by any other cogent evidence we are unable to put any reliance on this mere statement of this PW 1 only. 

 68. So, it appears that none of the alleged conduct of accused Hasan is strong enougn for making any inference as to his alleged conspiracy for causing rape and murder of Shajneen. It is true that in most cases proof of conspiracy is largely inferential, but the inference must be founded on strong facts and surrounding circumstances. In this case the prosecution has totally failed to prove any such strong facts and circumstances for making inference as to the alleged conspiracy of accused Hasan with the other accused Shahid, Badal, Minu and Parveen for causing rape and murder of Shajneen. 

 69. As against accused I3adal, as we have already pointed out above, there is no evidence at all to prove his involvement in the alleged occurrence. The confessing accused Shahid did not name even this accused Badal in either of his two confessional statements. The PW 12 Sufia though deposed before the Adalat to the effect that accused Minu and Parveen told her that accused Hasan made a plan to cause rape and murder of Shajneen by some of his trusted persons including this accused Badal, but none of the accused Minu and Parveen, in their 164 statements, named this accused Badal even. In the subsequent 164 statement of accused Minu though she named accused Hasan, accused Shahid and accused Humayun but she did not name accused Badal. PW 12 Sufia though deposed before the Adalat to the effect also that on the next day of occurrence accused Badal threatened her not to disclose about that conspiracy to anybody, but she did not make any such statement to JO and for this reason we cannot rely on her such statement which she made before the Adalat for the first time. The PW 13 Muslem Howlader though has deposed to the effect only that in the night of occurrence lie heard accused Badal telling accused Hasan over telephone that security lights were off and all other things were done correctly, but this evidence of PW 13 only, in the absence of any other evidence or facts and circumstances showing involvement of accused Badal in the alleged conspiracy allegedly hatched by accused Hasan, cannot prove at all the charge framed against accused Badal. 

 70. As against the other 2 accused Estema Khatun @ Minu and Parveen also we do not find any evidence at all. As regards these two accused the evidence of PW 12 Sufia is that these two accused told her that accused Hasan made a conspiracy with other accused persons, namely, Shahid, Badal, Humayun and Shaniram to commit rape and murder of Shajneen. The PW 12 Sufia did not depose to the effect that these two accused Minu and Parveen told her that they themselves also were involved in that conspiracy, rather according to PW 12 Sufia these two accused persons knew only about the alleged conspiracy of accused Hasan with the other four accused persons named above. The evidence of PW 12 does not tell also that these two accused persons were involved in any way in the rape and murder of Shajneen. If the knowledge only about the conspiracy makes these two accused Minu and Parveen liable in any way for the rape and murder of Shajneen then why not the PW 12 Sufia also was made an accused in this case, who also had the same knowledge of alleged conspiracy and kept that secret till long after rape and murder of Shajneen. Accused Minu though has made an alleged confessional statement under section 164 of the Criminal Procedure Code, we have already discussed above that in that alleged confessional statement accused Minu stated to the effect only that she being threatened by accused Hasan was compelled to remain standing in front of the dining room at the time of occurrence. This statement of accused Minu cannot make her liable at all for the rape and murder of Shajneen. Save and except this solitary statement of accused Minu herself in her 164 statement there is no evidence at all against this accused Minu. In none of the confessional statements of accused Shahid there is anything showing any sort of involvement of accused Minu in the alleged occurrence. 

 72. The prosecution has adduced some evidence telling that in the night of occurrence these accused Parveen and Minu made some inconsistent statements and has contended that these inconsistent statements of accused Minu and Parveen indicate that they were involved in the rape and murder of Shajneen. But we are unable to accept this contention. We have examined the evidence of PWs 8 and 10 who have deposed to the effect that being interrogated by some guests these 2 accused sometimes told that they saw accused Shahid committing rape on the victim, but subsequently they told that they knew nothing about the occurrence. We do not find these alleged inconsistent statements of these two accused that much inconsistent for indicating their involve-ment in the rape and murder of Shajneen. Had there been any involvement of these two accused persons in the rape and murder of Shajneen they would not have named accused Shahid at all. Rather, we think that it was very much natural for them, the maid servants, that though they named Shahid- their colleague at the first instance, but subsequently they tried to suppress the name of accused Shahid. However, in their 164 statements made on the very next day of the occurrence both these two accused Minu and Parveen stated to the effect that entering into bedroom of Shajneen accused Parveen saw- accused Shahid committing rape on Shajneen. 

 73. The prosecution has adduced some evidence stating that after his arrest accused Shahid was brought by police to the PO house twice and at that time accused Shahid made some extra judicial confessional statement implicating himself and other accused persons in the rape and murder of Shajneen. But the High Court Division rightly did not put any reliance on those alleged extra judicial confessional statement of accused Shahid for the reason that those were made in presence of police. The High Court Division rightly discarded those alleged extra judicial confessional statement or accused Shahid. 

 74. However, considering the evidence and facts and circumstances discussed above we find that in this case the prosecution could not prove the charge against accused Hasan, Badal, Estema Khatun @ Minu and Parveen beyond all reasonable doubt. 

 "In the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Case No.42 of 1999 a prima facie case has been made out against these two petitioners under sections 6(1)/14 of the Ain and not under section 6(2) of the Ain. It is not the case of the prosecution that the murder has been committed during rape. It is a clear case of rape and then murder. These are two distinct and separate offences. So question of double jeopardy does not arise. The High Court Division considered the case of these two petitioners and correctly directed the Adalat to frame charge under sections 6(1)/14 of the Ain against these two petitioners and there is no illegality and wrong in the same." 

 77. From the above quoted section 6(2) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995 it is clear that causing of death of any woman or child after committing rape on her is a punishable offence under Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995. In the present case the prosecution's clear case is that the victim Shajneen was raped and then her murder was caused. In this case it has also been proved beyond all reasonable doubt that accused Shahid committed rape on victim Shajneen and at the time of commission of rape since victim Shajneen tried to resist she was inflicted several injuries by sharp cutting weapon by the accused Shahid which ultimately caused her death instan-taneously. These above acts of accused Shahid i.e. commission of rape on viction Shajneen and also causing her death at that time clearly comes within perview of section 6(2) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995 which has clearly stated “----ধর্ষণ করার পর কোন শিশু বা নারীর মৃত্যু ঘটান-----” 

 78. The above quoted sections 6(1) and (2) clearly tell that if any person commits rape on any child or woman that will be punishable under sub-section (1) of section 6 and if any person, after committing rape on any child or woman causes her death also that will be punishable under sub-section (2) of section 6 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995. So, evidently the above quoted earlier observations of this Division in criminal petition for leave to appeal No. 177 of 1999 was not correct. Since in this case also murder of the victim was caused after commission of rape on her this offence comes within the perview of section 6(2) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995. So, the earlier observations of this Division to the effect that this case comes under section 6(1) and not under section 6(2) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995 requires to be reviewed. Causing of murder of any child or woman after committing rape on her is an offence which clearly comes under perview of section 6(2) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995 which has made these two offences of rape and murder punishable with one sentence of death. In view of this section 6(2) of this Ain of 1995 it cannot be said that the commission of rape and thereafter causing of death of rape victim by the rapist are two distinct and separate offences. These offences were committed in course of some transaction. Since Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995 by its section 6(2) has made these two offences punishable with one sentence of death and since this Ain of 1995, has been given overriding effect these two offences i.e. commission of rape and thereafter causing death of the victim of rape cannot be said "two distinct and separate offences". So, we review the above quoted observations and decision of this Division and hold that the commission of rape and thereafter murder of the victim of rape by the rapist is punishable under section 6(2) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995. 

 79. In this connection it needs to mention here that the Adalat, as per direction of the High Court Division, which was affirmed by this Division, though framed charge against the accused Shahid under section 6(1) and against the other accused persons under sections 6(1)114 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995 also the Adalat did not set aside or cancel the earlier charges which it framed against the accused Shahid under section 6(2) and against other accused persons under sections 6(2)/14 of that Ain of 1995. The judgment of the Adalat shows that both the charges under sections 6(1), 6(1)/14 and 6(2), 6(2)/14 were kept existent. So the argument made from the side of the accused persons before us to the effect that since charge was framed under section 6(1) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995 the conviction under section 6(2), which provides for graver punishment, cannot sustain in law has got no substance. 

 80. The next question is whether the earlier case under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code started on the basis of the FIR lodged by the father of the victim on 24-4-1998 can proceed further. It has already been stated above that immediately after the occurrence Latifur Rahman, the father of the victim Shajneen lodged an FIR with Gulshan PS on 24-4-1998 narrating the rape and murder of victim Shajneen and also suspecting accused Shahid to have caused rape and murder of Shajneen and on the basis of that FIR Gulshan PS. Case No. 73 dated 24-4-1998 was started and the CID officer Mozibur Rahman (the informant and JO of the present case), after conducting investigation in that case submitted charge sheet against all the accused persons of the present case under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and that case was ultimately transmitted to the court of sessions for trial and it was registered as Sessions Case No. 95 of 1999 and in that case charge under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code was framed against all the accused persons. It should be mentioned here that in that case also the present accused Shahid pleaded guilty. However that Sessions Case No.95 of 1999 was stayed by an order of the High Court Division passed in the above mentioned Criminal Appeal No. 645 of 1999 and the Appellate Division also affirmed that order of the High Court Division. However our clear observation is that 10 of that case, namely Mozibur Rahman, a CID Officer (the informant and IO of the present case) has committed a great wrong and illegality in submitting charge sheet in that case under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and in initiating a separate case (the present one) under the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995. In that earlier case, in the very FIR it was clearly mentioned that victim Shajneen was raped before murder. Moreover in that case, within a few days of lodging of FIR, the accused Shahid made confessional statement before a Magistrate, 1st class clearly stating to the effect that he entered into the bedroom of Shajneen with the intention to commit rape on her and he also committed rape on her, but since Shajneen resisted he inflicted several blows on different parts of her body with a sharp cutting knife which caused the death of Shajneen. The FIR and also this confessional statement of accused Shahid clearly brought that case within the ambit of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995 and as such the I0 ought to have submitted charge sheet in that case under the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995. But without doing so the I0 has most illegally lodged a separate FIR several months after the occurrence and also after completion of investigation of the earlier case. It appears that this IO, at that relevant time was in the rank of Assistant Superintendent of Police. Inspite of being a high ranked Officer this IO, was very much ignorant of laws which he ought to have known. This IO, evidently did not bother even to consult the public prosecutor or any other lawyer before filing two separate charge sheets in two different cases for the same offence. His activity appears to be over zealous and his motives are unclear. Needless to say, his illegal action has caused a chain of illegal procedural defects resulting in waste of court time, harassment and expense. Such action of a relatively high ranking officer is deplorable and he ought to be reprimanded by his higher authority.
